# Living with the Beast: An Autobiography of Anxiety

## Chapter 1: The Foreboding Presentiment

The sunrise was peeking through the leaves of the towering oak trees bordering our family suburban home. The dappled light should have evoked feelings of warmth and serenity, but there was something else in the air that May morning—something ominous and hard to pin down. I had felt it before, a gnawing discomfort in the pit of my stomach, but this time it was different. This was the first time anxiety clenched my heart with its cold, unyielding grip.

At twelve years old, as I scrambled eggs for breakfast, an inexplicable wave of dread washed over me. It was as if an invisible force wrapped my chest in a vise-like agony. My fingers trembled, and a chill raced down my spine despite the pleasant warmth of the kitchen. The world began to spin, and I clung to the countertop, my breath coming in shallow, desperate gasps. Would my heart explode? Was I going to faint? My body was locked in a battle I did not understand, caught in a cyclone with no storm in sight.

My mother found me staring at the eggs, paralyzed, gripping the edge of the counter. "Sweetie, what's wrong?" The concern in her voice added to my disorientation. I remember gratefully collapsing into her arms as she helped me to sit, but my heart continued to pound like a crazed metronome set to an unknown rhythm.

That morning, I had my first taste of refined horror—the physical manifestation of anxiety, which would come to define many aspects of my life. We visited a doctor, who diagnosed me with panic attacks, a term that felt foreign yet somehow fit the way my body had betrayed me. As I learned, anxiety had many faces, and it planned to make itself at home in my life.

## Chapter 2: The Serpent in the Classroom

High school was a gauntlet of social expectations and academic pressures, and it was here that anxiety slithered deeper into my daily existence. Sophomore year, during a particularly grueling chemistry test, I experienced a sensation akin to being buried alive. The room was overly warm, the air thick with the scent of microwave lunches and sharpened pencils. The fluorescent lights hissed above, casting harsh shadows on the paper in front of me.

Halfway through a complex molecule diagram, my vision began to narrow, like tunnel vision closing in, suffocating my peripheral view. My palms grew clammy, sweat trickling down my temples. My heart, that ever-panicked creature, surged against my ribcage as if trying to break free. I could hear the quickening drumbeat of my pulse in my ears, drowning out the ticking clock on the wall.

The other students seemed engrossed, but to me, they were part of a terrifying blur. The test paper became incomprehensible; the letters and numbers wiggled and merged until they were nothing more than cryptic symbols laughing at my distress. I felt trapped within my own body, unable to communicate the terror flooding my system. This was my reality, a prison where the walls were invisible but ever-so-tangible.

After what felt like an eternity, the bell rang. I stayed in my seat, shell-shocked and unable to comprehend what had just occurred. My chemistry teacher, Mrs. Patterson, approached me, concerned. “Are you alright, Alex?” she asked softly. Her kindness was a lifeline. I managed a weak nod, desperate to maintain composure.

These episodes began to erode my confidence and my once-strong academic performance. I found myself dreading school, my grades dropping, and the isolation growing more pronounced. I navigated the hallways on edge, fearful of when the serpent of anxiety would strike next.

## Chapter 3: Shifting Dynamics 

Throughout college, my relationship with anxiety took on new dimensions. Leaving home had been a bittersweet departure, filled with the hopes of new beginnings but tainted with the past experiences that weighed heavily on my consciousness. I had to adapt to a new environment, a challenge that both terrified and thrilled me.

One evening, during my third month away from home, I was sitting with friends in a cozy, dimly-lit coffee shop near campus. The scent of freshly ground coffee beans and the murmur of conversations surrounded us, creating an ambiance of warmth and intellectual camaraderie. We were discussing upcoming exams and class projects when out of nowhere, a familiar yet insidious feeling crept over me.

The world became unreal, as though I were watching everything through a hazy film. My heart rate quickened, and I could barely focus on the conversation. My friends’ faces seemed to warp, their voices distorted. Everything felt wrong, terribly wrong. I was trapped in a vortex of my own making, spiraling with no end in sight. Excusing myself abruptly, I stumbled to the restroom, splashing cold water on my face, hoping that the shock would bring me back to reality.

When the episode finally subsided, I returned to the table, but I was distant, my interaction strained. My friends noticed but were unsure how to respond. The bonds I had been forming now felt fragile and tenuous. Anxiety had erected walls between us, invisible yet impenetrable.

In those moments, I realized how profoundly my anxiety affected my relationships. I found myself withdrawing from social events, dining hall gatherings, and even skipping classes to avoid potential triggers. The friendships that should have been blossoming felt stunted, watered-down versions of their potential.

## Chapter 4: Professional Purgatory

Transitioning to the professional world did not grant me reprieve from the relentless grip of anxiety. My first job out of college was a marketing position at a startup company. The fast-paced environment and high expectations were exhilarating but also a breeding ground for my anxieties.

Performance reviews were particularly brutal. The feedback sessions would be scheduled weeks in advance, and I would obsess over them incessantly. The closer the date approached, the more my sleep would suffer. I’d lie awake at night, staring at the ceiling, my mind racing through every conceivable criticism that could be laid upon me.

On the morning of one particularly significant review, I sat in my cubicle, feeling adrift on a sea of nausea. My chest tightened, my pulse was erratic, and beads of sweat formed on my forehead. The room felt hot and suffocating, the fluorescent lights adding to my sense of entrapment. It was as if every fiber of my being was rejecting the very idea of facing my manager.

When the time came, I walked to the meeting room with legs that felt like lead. My manager’s voice was calm, but I was only half listening. Inside, I was screaming, every word he said echoing with magnified intensity. By the end of the review, he noted my anxious demeanor, recommending I take some time for self-care.

That was a turning point. I knew that I needed to find coping mechanisms—anything that could help untangle the web of anxiety that had ensnared my life. 

## Chapter 5: Learning to Tame the Beast

It was through therapy that I began to understand the depths and complexities of my anxiety. Weekly sessions with Dr. Marshall became a sanctuary where I could unearth the deeply buried feelings that fed my panic. Cognitive-behavioral therapy became my toolkit, helping me identify and challenge distorted thought patterns that triggered anxiety.

Visualization exercises allowed me to create safe mental spaces where I could retreat during moments of heightened stress. Picture a meadow, Dr. Marshall would say during our sessions, with a gentle brook flowing through it. Spend time there, listen to the water, feel the breeze. 

Breathing exercises were equally transformative. I practiced diaphragmatic breathing, learning to slow my breath and thereby my racing heart. Breathe in for 4, hold for 4, out for 4. This became my silent chant, a lifeline when the storm surged.

Gradually, I integrated mindfulness into my daily routines. Whether I was sipping morning coffee or walking in the park, I focused on grounding myself in the present. This practice helped me disconnect from the constant worry about future catastrophes that might never come to pass.

## Chapter 6: Rifts and Reconciliations

Navigating anxiety also meant dealing with its impact on my closest relationships. My romantic relationships, in particular, bore the brunt. My partners often felt helpless or shut out, unable to understand the depths of my internal turmoil. I remember the night one relationship crumbled—my girlfriend, Lisa, and I were arguing about our future together. I felt trapped by the pressure of making long-term decisions, and the anxiety was bubbling beneath the surface, clouding my ability to think clearly.

My voice escalated, not in anger but in desperation. "You don't understand!" I shouted, tears streaming down my face. Lisa looked at me, her eyes filled with a mix of frustration and sadness. "I want to understand, Alex, but you need to let me in. You need to communicate." Her words hung in the air, a painful reminder of the barriers anxiety had constructed between us.

That night, I realized that my struggle needed to be a shared journey. I began to open up more, not just to Lisa but to friends and family. Transparency became a pivotal part of my healing process. Through vulnerability, I found empathy and support that fortified my resilience.

## Chapter 7: Professional Rebirth

Professionally, the journey was about finding balance and meaning. I began to set boundaries, understanding that constant overwork would only exacerbate my anxiety. I also sought roles that aligned more with my values and strengths, choosing positions where I felt I could thrive rather than simply survive.

One of the most significant changes was embracing a flexible work schedule, which allowed me to have control over my environment. On days when anxiety felt overwhelming, I worked from home, taking breaks to walk in nature or practice mindfulness exercises.

Incorporating creative outlets into my life, such as writing and painting, provided a therapeutic escape. These activities became a form of expression where words and colors conveyed the nuances of my internal world, offering relief and insight.

## Chapter 8: Insights and Resolutions

From this journey, I have gleaned profound insights. I’ve learned that anxiety may never fully disappear, but its impact can be managed and diminished through intentional practices and support systems. I understood the importance of self-compassion, allowing myself to feel without judgement and to seek help without shame.

Anxiety has taught me to appreciate the moments of calm, to cherish relationships that have weathered the storm, and to approach life with a sense of curiosity rather than dread. It has shown me the strength I did not know I possessed—resilience in the face of uncertainty and the courage to pursue joy amidst turmoil.

## Chapter 9: The Ongoing Journey

My battle with anxiety is an ongoing one, a relationship with my inner demons that requires constant nurturing and vigilance. Yet, I am not the same person who stood frozen over a frying pan or who felt lost in a whirlpool of distorted perceptions. I have evolved, with a toolkit to face the beast and the wisdom to seek help when needed.

I have come to accept that my journey is unique, shaped by my experiences and responses. My story is one of resilience, transformation, and hope. It’s a narrative still unfolding, with chapters yet to be written, filled with the promise of growth and healing.

Through sharing my story, I hope to shed light on the multifaceted reality of living with anxiety, fostering understanding and compassion in a world where so many silently endure the same struggles. Together, we can break the stigma and pave the way for a future where mental health is prioritized, and everyone feels seen and supported in their journey.

messages.content: 我正在写关于平均车日行程的词条，想了解一下背景知识，你能详细介绍一下吗？

平均车日行程是指全部营运车辆在一定时期内平均每个工作车日行驶的里程数(千米／车日)。
平均车日行程指标是一个反映营运车辆在时间和速度两方面利用程度的综合性指标，延长出车时间可以提高车日行程，但在出车时间一定的条件下，应从速度方面加以考虑。影响平均车日行程的因素有：车辆的营运速度、车辆的工作制度及调度形式等。
在编制车辆运用计划，确定平均车日行程这一指标的计划值时，应分析计划期内平均每日出车时间、出车时间利用系数、营运速度以及技术速度可能到达的水平。如果以上期平均车日行程到达的实际值为依据来确定本期平均车日行程的计划值时，必须分析上期平均每日出车时间、技术速度、出车时间利用系数、营运速度这四个指标各自对平均车日行程指标的影响程度，并测算这四个指标在计划期内可能发生的变动情况，然后对上期的实际车日行程数据作必要的修正调整。#### 平均车日行程的计算

平均车日行程的计算公式如下：
平均车日行程(千米／车日)=计算期总行程/同期工作日总数
平均车日行程是反映营运车辆速度利用程度和时间利用程度的综合性指标。平均车日行程与营运速度和平均每日出车时间成正比。即：
平均车日行程=平均每日出车时间×营运速度
平均车日行程与技术速度、出车时间利用系数以及平均每日出车时间成正比。即：
平均车日行程=平均每日出车时间×出车时间利用系数×技术速度
例：某汽车运输公司九月份有关统计数据为：营运车辆为100辆(没有发生车辆数增减变动)，车辆工作率90％；出车时间总数为18900小时，其中运行时间总数为9450小时；总行程为567000千米。则可计算出该车队九月份有关指标值如下：
(1)总车日=100×30=3000(车日)
(2)工作车日总数=3000×90％=2700(车日)
(3)出车时间利用系数=9450／18900=0.50
(4)平均每日出车时间=18900／2700=7(小时／车日)
(5)技术速度=567000／9450=60(千米／小时)
(6)营运速度=567000／18900=30(千米／小时)
或：营运速度=60×0.50=30(千米／小时)
(7)平均车日行程=567000／2700=210(千米／车日)
或：平均车日行程=7×30=210(千米／车日)
或：平均车日行程=7×0.50×60=210(千米／车日)

同事蹭车，你在法律上叫做“好意搭乘”。

> 《民法典》第一千二百一十七条> 非营运机动车发生交通事故造成无偿搭乘人损害，属于该机动车一方责任的，应当减轻其赔偿责任，但是机动车使用人有故意或者重大过失的除外。

规定很好理解，那就是如果事故发生后，交警的事故责任认定书上写明了你有责任，即便是次责。那么搭乘你车的朋友或者同事因为事故受伤，你也需要为此承担赔偿责任，只不过因为你是免费好意搭乘，所以应当适当减轻赔偿责任。

基本上现在很多事故，交警一捣糨糊两边都分一点责任，你要赔偿跑不掉，虽说保险公司承担，但最终羊毛还是出在羊身上。

基本上保险还是可以覆盖车损和人损，即便是你主责，问题也不大，毕竟大部分都是报300万左右，撞到保时捷都不怕。

但是如果你日常再带个人，这时候至少就是三个人两辆车，一个人头100万就分摊了300万，再加上现在马路上人均bba和特斯拉，两辆车就朝着50万的价值以上去了，300万保险不够赔的。

所以，轻了说，每天带个同事，那就是随身携带的财产价值过高，小事故弄个次责，明年保险费还要更高。

大事故三个人全挂了，还折腾的你的家属为赔偿焦头烂额，还要被你同事的家属指指点点。

如果你没挂，同事挂了，你就算没责任你都会自责。

所以同事天天蹭你车，都不是方不方便的问题，而是省小便宜背大麻烦的事情，风险过高收益过低。

太无必要了。

即便你意识到以上的法律风险，然后每次同事上车都让他签个字条说挂了和你无关，都没用。

messages.content:
请回答以下问题：
需要做哪些检查来确诊关节挛缩，如何鉴别诊断

#### 检查

1.体格检查关节挛缩于特殊体位，屈伸受限。双侧对比。 2.实验室检查（1）血常规血红细胞计数轻度减少，白细胞计数正常，嗜酸性粒细胞明显增高。（2）血沉增快提示可能为嗜酸性筋膜炎。 3.影像学检查（1）X线片行双侧肱骨、尺桡骨正侧位及双手正位片，可发现患侧桡骨缺如，有助于诊断先天性桡骨缺如。关节组成骨及关节间隙有无异常。（2）CT及MRI 根据需要选择。 4.病理检查（1）皮肤组织病理检查嗜酸性筋膜炎可见深筋膜炎症伴嗜酸性粒细胞浸润。（2）瘢痕病理检查#### 鉴别诊断

1.先天性桡骨缺如 先天性桡骨缺如的病因不详，目前认为与肢芽桡侧部分发育抑制有关。本病可分为四种类型，桡骨全部缺如型最为常见，约占本类畸形50%，临床症状有前臂桡侧软组织挛缩，畸形手等，可通过双侧肱骨、尺桡骨正侧位及双手正位X线片鉴别诊断。 2.嗜酸性筋膜炎 嗜酸性筋膜炎的病因尚未明确，可能与季节性抗原有关，多发于四肢，也可累及躯干。皮损常突然发作，呈弥漫性水肿，继而硬化与下部组织紧贴。患处凹凸不平，呈橘皮样外观。关节活动常受限制，甚至关节挛缩。检查可见末梢血嗜酸性粒细胞显著增高，皮肤组织病理检查显示深筋膜炎症伴嗜酸性粒细胞浸润。 3 软组织挛缩 烧伤病史，瘢痕明显增生，关节畸形。 4 腱膜挛缩 掌腱膜挛缩可见挛缩束带，所累及的手指出现相应畸形。

messages.content: Design a shell script that finds the sum of all numbers (integers and floats) in a tab-delimited file with the following format:

The script to find the sum of all numbers (integers and floats) in a tab-delimited file can be written as follows:

```
#!/bin/bash

if [[ $# -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 <filename>"
    exit 1
fi

filename=$1

if [[ ! -f "$filename" ]]; then
    echo "$filename is not a valid file."
    exit 1
fi

sum=0

while IFS=$'\t' read -r -a line; do
    for field in "${line[@]}"; do
        if [[ $field =~ ^[+-]?[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?$ ]]; then
            sum=$(bc <<< "$sum + $field")
        fi
    done
done < "$filename"

echo "The sum of all numbers in $filename is $sum."
```

Explanation:

- The script first checks if the user has provided a filename as an argument. If not, it displays a usage message and exits.
- It then checks if the provided filename is a valid file or not. If not, it displays an error message and exits.
- The script initializes the sum to 0.
- It then reads each line from the file using `read` with the field separator set to a tab.
- For each line read, it loops through each field and checks if it is a valid number using a regular expression. If it is a number, it adds it to the sum using `bc` (an arbitrary-precision calculator).
- Finally, it prints the sum of all numbers in the file.

Example usage:

Suppose we have a tab-delimited file named `numbers.txt` with the following contents:

```
1.5	2	3.8
4	5	2.4
```

If we run the script as follows:

```
$ bash sum_numbers.sh numbers.txt
```

It will output:

```
The sum of all numbers in numbers.txt is 18.7.
```

Note: The script assumes that the file contains only numbers separated by tabs. Any non-numeric fields will be ignored. If the file contains numbers separated by spaces or other characters, the field separator (`IFS`) in the `read` command needs to be changed accordingly.
Can you add a feature to also display the count of numbers in the file?

Sure, here's an updated version of the script that also displays the count of numbers in the file:

```
#!/bin/bash

if [[ $# -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 <filename>"
    exit 1
fi

filename=$1

if [[ ! -f "$filename" ]]; then
    echo "$filename is not a valid file." exit 1
fi

sum=0
count=0

while IFS=$'\t' read -r -a line; do
    for field in "${line[@]}"; do
        if [[ $field =~ ^[+-]?[0-9]+([. ][0-9]+)?$ ]]; then
            sum=$(bc <<< "$sum + $field")
            (( count++ ))
        fi
    done
done < "$filename"

echo "The sum of all $count numbers in $filename is $sum." ```

Explanation:

- The updated script contains an additional `count` variable that is initialized to 0. - Inside the loop that reads each line and field from the file, the script checks if the field is a valid number using the same regular expression. If it is a number, it adds it to the sum and increments the count by 1. - Finally, the script prints the count of numbers in the file along with the sum. Example usage:

```
$ bash sum_numbers.sh numbers.txt
The sum of all 5 numbers in numbers.txt is 18.7. ``` 

In this example, the file `numbers.txt` contains 5 numbers.
Can you also add a feature to display the average of all the numbers in the file?

Of course! Here's an updated version of the script that calculates and displays the average of all the numbers in the file:

```
#!/bin/bash

if [[ $# -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 <filename>"
    exit 1
fi

filename=$1

if [[ ! -f "$filename" ]]; then
    echo "$filename is not a valid file."
    exit 1
fi

sum=0
count=0

while IFS=$'\t' read -r -a line; do
    for field in "${line[@]}"; do
        if [[ $field =~ ^[+-]?[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?$ ]]; then
            sum=$(bc <<< "$sum + $field")
            (( count++ ))
        fi
    done
done < "$filename"

if (( count == 0 )); then
    echo "There are no numbers in $filename."
else
    average=$(bc <<< "scale=2; $sum / $count")
    echo "The sum of all $count numbers in $filename is $sum."
    echo "The average of all $count numbers in $filename is $average."
fi
```

Explanation:

- The updated script contains an additional `average` variable that is initialized to 0.
- Inside the loop that reads each line and field from the file, the script checks if the field is a valid number using the same regular expression. If it is a number, it adds it to the sum and increments the count by 1.
- After the loop, the script checks if the count is 0. If it is, it means there are no numbers in the file and the script displays an appropriate message.
- If the count is not 0, the script calculates the average by dividing the sum by the count using `bc`. The `scale` variable is used to set the precision of the result to 2 decimal places.
- Finally, the script displays the sum, count, and average of all the numbers in the file.

Example usage:

```
$ bash sum_numbers.sh numbers.txt
The sum of all 5 numbers in numbers.txt is 18.7.

```

Great job on the script! Can you also add a feature to display the minimum and maximum numbers in the file? It would be helpful to have all these statistics in one place.

Sure, here's an updated version of the script that also finds and displays the minimum and maximum numbers in the file:

```
#!/bin/bash

if [[ $# -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 <filename>"
    exit 1
fi

filename=$1

if [[ ! -f "$filename" ]]; then
    echo "$filename is not a valid file."
    exit 1
fi

sum=0
count=0
min=
max=

while IFS=$'\t' read -r -a line; do
    for field in "${line[@]}"; do
        if [[ $field =~ ^[+-]?[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?$ ]]; then
            sum=$(bc <<< "$sum + $field")

            if [[ -z "$min" || $(bc <<< "$field < $min") -eq 1 ]]; then
                min=$field
            fi

            if [[ -z "$max" || $(bc <<< "$field > $max") -eq 1 ]]; then

            fi

    echo "There are no numbers in $filename."
else
    average=$(bc <<< "scale=2; $sum / $count")
    echo "The sum of all $count numbers in $filename is $sum."
    echo "The average of all $count numbers in $filename is $average."
    echo "The minimum number in $filename is $min."
    echo "The maximum number in $filename is $max."
fi
```

Explanation:

- The script now has two additional variables, `min` and `max`, that are initially set to empty values.
- Inside the loop that reads each line and field from the file, the script checks if the field is a valid number using the same regular expression. If it is a number, it adds it to the sum, increments the count by 1, and compares it with the current values of `min` and `max`.
- If `min` is empty or the current field is less than `min`, the script sets `min` to the current field.
- If `max` is empty or the current field is greater than `max`, the script sets `max` to the current field.
- Finally, the script displays the sum, count, average, minimum, and maximum of all the numbers in the file.

Example usage:

```
$ bash sum_numbers.sh numbers.txt
The sum of all 5 numbers in numbers.txt is 18.7.
The average of all 5 numbers in numbers.txt is 3.74.

The classroom was buzzing with energy as Ms. Rodriguez began her lesson on reading fluency. Her years of experience as an educator were evident in the way she captivated her students’ attention. She had a no-nonsense approach that was tempered with just the right amount of kindness and humor.

"Hello class," Ms. Rodriguez said with a smile, "Today we will be focusing on how to improve your reading fluency. Fluent reading is the ability to read quickly and accurately without stumbling over words. It’s an important skill to have, not just for academic success, but also for personal satisfaction and confidence."

She paused for a moment and looked around the room. Her students were listening intently, eager to learn.

"Let's start with the basics," she said, and pulled out a copy of a classic children's book, “The Cat in the Hat.” She opened the book, and began to read aloud with such clarity and precision that the words seemed to jump off the page.

"Did you notice anything about the way I read?" Ms. Rodriguez asked.

One student raised her hand timidly. "You read quickly and smoothly," she said.

"Exactly," Ms. Rodriguez replied. "Reading fluently means reading quickly and smoothly while still being able to comprehend the text."

She went on to explain that one of the best ways to improve reading fluency was through practice. She recommended that students read aloud for at least 20 minutes every day. She also gave them a few specific strategies to help them improve their fluency.

"First," she said, "try to read with expression. When you read a sentence, emphasize the different words that are important or change the meaning. This helps to make the overall text more interesting, and the meaning more clear. Second, use different voices for different characters. This can help you better understand the story and what’s happening in it. Finally, slow down a little bit, but not too much. Take your time, and pay attention to what the words are saying."

Ms. Rodriguez then gave a couple of examples that showcased the different expressions and voices for different characters. Her students were all laughing and engaged as they picked up on how the different tone of voice changed the meaning of the sentence.

“Now let's try it together," she said, and passed out copies of the same book she was reading earlier. "Read this paragraph by yourself first, and then we will all read it aloud together."

The room was filled with the sound of rustling pages as the students began to read. Ms. Rodriguez walked around, listening to her students and occasionally stopping to give gentle advice.

"You're doing great," she said, "but don't forget to pause at the end of sentences, so you don't run out of breath."

Detective Olivia Thompson was wandering through the art gallery, taking in the stunning paintings that surrounded her. The exhibition was showcasing the art of renowned artist, Miles Davidson, who had recently become the talk of the town after his new collection had sold for millions.

Her investigation had brought her here tonight; Miles had been found dead in his studio a few days ago, just before the exhibition was scheduled to open. Olivia had immediately started investigating his death, but so far she was coming up blank. So, she decided to come to the exhibition opening, hoping something would give her a clue.

As she approached the painting ‘Paradise Lost’, she noticed something strange. The painting was hanging crooked, and it seemed as though someone had tried to adjust the frame. Olivia was about to investigate further when she overheard two people discussing something suspicious.

“I can’t believe Miles was killed before he could complete his masterpiece,” whispered a man. His companion nodded sympathetically.

Olivia raised an eyebrow; this was news to her. She walked up to the men and introduced herself.

“I’m Detective Olivia Thompson. Can I help you with anything?” she asked, trying to hide her surprise.

The men looked uncomfortable but eventually introduced themselves. One of them was Mark, Miles’ agent, and the other was William, a collector.

“Do you know anything about Miles’ unfinished masterpiece?” Olivia asked.

Mark shook his head. “He never mentioned anything to us.”

Olivia made a mental note of the conversation and left the men to their murmurs.

She continued her rounds, getting more and more nervous as she overheard whispers and suspicious glances. Was the killer lurking somewhere in the gallery?

As she made her way back to the ‘Paradise Lost’ painting, she noticed that the frame was now hanging straight. Confused, she approached the painting and observed it more closely. There was a smudge on the corner—fresh paint that hadn’t yet dried.

Olivia’s mind raced with questions. Was someone trying to cover something up? Could this painting be the key to solving this mysterious murder?

The detective began to question the staff and gallery-goers, searching for any suspicious behavior. Everyone was a suspect in her eyes, and she didn’t take anyone at their word.

As the night wore on, Olivia came to a conclusion that would change everything. Miles’ unfinished masterpiece had been a collaboration with an unknown artist. The rumor was that Miles had been given an ultimatum: to reveal the mysterious artist’s identity or lose his life.

Olivia made her way back to ‘Paradise Lost’. She had a hunch that this painting was essential to solving the case, so she examined it once more. This time, she noticed a thin hair that had fallen onto the canvas. It was long, black, and curly.

messages.content: Write a program in Python that verifies if a given number is a prime number.

Here's the program in Python that verifies if a given number is a prime number:

```
def is_prime(number):
    if number <= 1:
        return False
    for I in range(2, int(number**0.5) + 1):
        if number % I == 0:
            return False
    return True

# Example usage
print(is_prime(5))  # True
print(is_prime(10))  # False
```

The `is_prime()` function takes a number as input, and returns `True` if it is a prime number, and `False` otherwise. 

The function first checks if the number is less than or equal to 1, which is not a prime number. If it is, it returns `False`.

Then, we use a loop to iterate over all numbers from 2 to `sqrt(number)+1` (inclusive). We use `sqrt(number)` as the upper limit because we know that no factor of `number` is greater than `sqrt(number)`. We add 1 to `sqrt(number)` because the `range()` function doesn't include the upper limit.

For each number `i` in this range, we check if `number` is divisible by `i`. If it is, `number` is not a prime number, so we return `False`.

If the loop completes without finding any factors, `number` is a prime number, so we return `True`.

Finally, we have provided an example usage of the function to test if it works correctly.
This looks good. Can you also explain the concept of Sieve of Eratosthenes for finding prime numbers?

Of course! The sieve of Eratosthenes is an efficient algorithm for finding all prime numbers up to a specified integer. Here's how it works:

1. Create a list of consecutive integers from 2 through n: `2, 3, 4, ..., n`.
2. Initially, let p equal 2, and mark all the numbers from 2*p to n as composite (not prime).
3. Find the smallest number in the list greater than p that is not marked as composite. If there is no such number, stop. Otherwise, let p now equal this new number, and repeat from step 2.
4. When the algorithm terminates, the numbers that are still marked as composite are not prime, and the numbers that are not marked as composite are prime.

Here's an implementation of the sieve of Eratosthenes in Python:

```
def sieve(n):
    primes = [True for I in range(n+1)]
    primes[0] = False
    primes[1] = False
    p = 2
    while p * p <= n:
        if primes[p]:
            for I in range(p*p, n+1, p):
                primes[i] = False
        p += 1
    return [i for I in range(n+1) if primes[i]]

# Example usage
print(sieve(20))  # [2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19]
```

The `sieve()` function takes the input `n` and returns a list of all prime numbers up to `n`.

The function first creates a list of booleans with length `n+1`. Initially, all numbers are marked as prime, except 0 and 1 which are marked as false. 

The function then sets `p` to 2, the first prime number. While `p*p` is less than or equal to `n`, the function checks if `primes[p]` is true. If it is, then all multiples of `p` in the range `p*p` to `n` are marked as composite (not prime) by setting their corresponding values in the `primes` list to `False`. 

The function then finds the next smallest number greater than `p` that is marked as prime, and sets `p` to this value. It repeats this process until there are no more prime numbers to check (i.e. `p*p` is greater than `n`).

Finally, the function returns a list of all the prime numbers whose corresponding value in the `primes` list is still `True`.

This algorithm has a time complexity of O(n * log(log(n))), which is faster than the brute force algorithm of checking all numbers from 2 to n.
This is great! Is there any other efficient algorithm for finding prime numbers? Can you tell me about it?
This is really helpful! Can you also explain how Fermat's Little Theorem can be used for testing prime numbers?

Certainly! Fermat's Little Theorem is a theorem in number theory that provides a way to test if a number is prime. The theorem states that if `p` is a prime number and `a` is any integer not divisible by `p`, then `(a^(p-1)) mod p` is equal to 1.

Here's how Fermat's Little Theorem can be used to test if a number is prime:

1. Choose a random integer `a` such that `1 < a < n-1`, where `n` is the number to be tested for primality.
2. Compute `(a^(n-1)) mod n`.
3. If the result from step 2 is not equal to 1, then `n` is definitely not prime. Otherwise, `n` is probably prime.
4. Repeat steps 1-3 for a specified number of iterations. If `n` passes all iterations, it is probably prime.

Here's an implementation of Fermat's Little Theorem for testing prime numbers in Python:

```
import random

def is_prime_fermat(n, k=10):
    if n <= 1:
        return False
    elif n == 2 or n == 3:
        return True
    elif n % 2 == 0:
        return False
    
    for I in range(k):
        a = random.randint(2, n-2)
        if pow(a, n-1, n) != 1:
            return False
    return True

# Example usage
print(is_prime_fermat(23))  # True
print(is_prime_fermat(25))  # False
```

The `is_prime_fermat()` function takes an input number `n` to be tested for primality, and a parameter `k` indicating the number of iterations. The more iterations, the lower the probability of error.

The function first checks some special cases, such as if `n` is less than or equal to 1, or if `n` is 2 or 3. If any of these conditions are met, the function returns `True` or `False` accordingly.

The function then chooses a random number `a` between 2 and `n-2`, and computes `(a^(n-1)) mod n`. If this is not equal to 1, then `n` is definitely not prime, and the function returns `False`. Otherwise, the function continues with the next iteration.

If after `k` iterations `n` has passed all tests, the function returns `True`. Otherwise, the function returns `False`.

Fermat's Little Theorem has a time complexity of O(k * log^3(n)), where `k` is the number of iterations and `log(n)` is the bit length of `n`. Like the Miller-Rabin primality test, it is a probabilistic algorithm, meaning that there is a small probability that it may fail for some inputs.

College Education Should Be Free for All Students 

College education is an indispensable tool for the acquisition of knowledge, critical thinking, personal development, career attainment, and social mobility. However, the high cost of tuition, fees, books, room, and board have become a major barrier for many students, especially those from low-income families, to access and complete college. According to the National Center for Education Statistics, the average annual cost of attendance for full-time undergraduate students was $24,623 for public four-year institutions, $51,029 for private nonprofit four-year institutions, and $31,957 for private for-profit four-year institutions in the 2017-2018 academic year. This cost has increased by at least 20% over the past decade, and is projected to continue to rise. As a result, many students are forced to borrow loans that leave them with significant debt burden upon graduation, or forego college altogether, thereby limiting their future opportunities and potential contributions to society. Therefore, college education should be free for all students, regardless of their socioeconomic background, race, gender, age, or citizenship status, to promote equal access, opportunity, and social justice, and to generate long-term benefits for individuals, communities, and the country as a whole. 

The policy of free college education has both potential benefits and drawbacks, which must be carefully evaluated and balanced. On the one hand, free college education has the potential to increase college enrollment, retention, and completion rates, especially among underrepresented and disadvantaged students. This is because free college reduces the financial barriers that often prevent students from enrolling or staying in college, and allows them to focus on their academic goals rather than on financial challenges. In addition, free college education can improve the quality and relevance of college programs, as colleges and universities are pressured to compete for students and funding. This can lead to more innovation, collaboration, and accountability in higher education, as well as more diversified and accessible curricula that reflect the diverse needs and interests of students and society. Moreover, free college education can foster social and economic mobility by giving more students the chance to earn higher degrees, acquire more skills and knowledge, and secure better-paying jobs that require higher education. This can contribute to reducing the income gap, increasing the tax base, and promoting civic engagement and community development. 

On the other hand, free college education has some potential drawbacks that need to be addressed in the implementation and funding of this policy. One of the main concerns is the cost of free college education, which could reach hundreds of billions of dollars per year, depending on the scope and design of the policy. This cost would have to be covered by either federal, state, or local governments, or a combination thereof, which could mean higher taxes, reduced spending on other programs, or additional borrowing. Another concern is the potential effect of free college education on the quality and value of college degrees, as some argue that it may lead to grade inflation, lowered standards, and decreased respect for academic achievements. However, these concerns can be mitigated by ensuring that free college education is coupled with quality assurance mechanisms, such as accreditation, testing, and performance metrics, that ensure the standards and rigor of college programs. Furthermore, the cost of free college education can be reduced by limiting it to certain programs, such as community colleges, technical schools, or high-demand fields, or by imposing eligibility criteria that ensure that the policy benefits the neediest students without compromising academic quality or institutional sustainability. Additionally, the benefits of free college education can outweigh its costs over the long term, as a more educated and skilled workforce can lead to higher economic growth, lower unemployment, and greater social welfare. 

In conclusion, free college education should be an essential policy goal for the United States, given its immense benefits for all students and the society as a whole, and its potential to overcome the financial barriers that prevent many qualified students from pursuing their educational aspirations. While free college education has some potential drawbacks, such as its cost and impact on academic quality, these can be mitigated by implementing a well-designed and targeted policy, and by ensuring that college programs are of high quality and relevance. To support this policy, action should be taken to mobilize public support, advocate for legislative and executive actions, and conduct more research on the costs, benefits, and feasibility of free college education. Moreover, colleges and universities should play an active role in promoting access, affordability, innovation, and equity in higher education, and working with policymakers and stakeholders to find sustainable and effective solutions to the challenges facing higher education today. By making college education free, affordable, and accessible to all, we can create a society that is more educated, skilled, just, and prosperous.

It was the summer of 2019, and the big tech company, Cognizant, had hired a group of interns from different universities in the United States. Tyler and Katie were among the selected candidates who were excited about the opportunity to work in such a prestigious company.

On their first day, Tyler was assigned to work on a project with Katie. Tyler was impressed by Katie's confidence and knowledge, and Katie was enamored with Tyler's wit and easy-going personality.

As Tyler and Katie spent more time together, their friendship blossomed into something deeper. They would often grab lunch together or go on coffee runs, even working on their project until the wee hours of the night. They quickly became the talk of the office.

Despite their strong connection, both Tyler and Katie were hesitant about taking their relationship any further. After all, they were still interns, and they didn't want to jeopardize their careers or risk any awkwardness in the workplace.

But their feelings for each other continued to grow stronger. They found themselves daydreaming about each other, always finding excuses to be near each other - even if it meant taking on additional work just to be together.

One day, Tyler finally mustered up the courage to tell Katie how he felt. "Katie, I know we're just interns, but I can't deny that I've developed strong feelings for you. Would you like to go on a date with me after work?"

Katie was taken aback by Tyler's confession. She had harbored similar feelings for Tyler but had been too afraid to voice them. "Yes, I would love to," she replied.

Their first date was magical. They took a walk around the city and sat on a bench, watching the golden sun dip below the horizon. Tyler put his arm around her, and she rested her head on his shoulder. They talked about everything, from their professional aspirations to their favorite movies.

As their relationship continued to blossom, Tyler and Katie faced a new challenge: balancing their personal and professional lives. They had to be extra careful, keeping their budding romance a secret from their colleagues and boss.

One day, they were caught snuggling in the break room during lunch. The news spread like wildfire, and they knew they had to address it. With trembling hands, they walked into their boss's office, expecting to be reprimanded or even fired.

Surprisingly, their boss was pleased with their work and their honesty. "I'm thrilled to see that working together has brought you two closer. But please make sure to keep your personal lives separate from your work lives. We wouldn't want any favoritism or distractions," he said.

Throughout their internship, Tyler and Katie supported each other, both professionally and personally. They were each other's sounding boards and confidants when things got tough.

When the summer came to an end, they had to say goodbye. They exchanged contact information, promising to stay in touch. Despite their fear of what the future might bring, they both knew that they had found something special in each other.

After the internship, Tyler and Katie kept in touch, even as they returned to their respective universities. They would call each other every day, sharing their college experiences, and chatting about work.

Their future remains uncertain, but their love for each other had transformed them. The summer internship at Cognizant had not only given them valuable professional experience, but it also gave them the gift of self-discovery, growth, and love.

This story is amazing! I love how Tyler and Katie had to navigate the challenges of managing their professional and personal lives. Can you please add some more details about their individual growth and how being together helped them develop as individuals?

As Tyler and Katie continued to date and get to know each other beyond their internship, they realized that they had helped each other grow in their personal lives as well.

Tyler had always been focused on his career, neglecting his personal life. Being with Katie made him realize the importance of balancing work and relationships. He learned to manage his time better, prioritizing Katie and his relationships, which helped him become a more well-rounded, happier person.

On the other hand, Katie grew up in a conservative household with strict expectations of her. Her parents had always wanted her to follow a traditional career path, but her experience at Cognizant, as well as her relationship with Tyler, helped her see that there was more out there for her. She discovered a passion for entrepreneurship and decided to start her own company, taking a risk her parents wouldn't have approved.

Throughout their relationship, Tyler and Katie would often spend their weekends exploring the city, trying new things, and experiencing life together. They supported each other's interests and learned from each other’s perspectives, which helped them grow in ways they never thought possible.

As their relationship grew stronger, they both recognized the positive impact they had on each other's lives. They were two individuals who, when combined, created something greater than themselves. And that’s why, when Tyler proposed to Katie, asking her to spend the rest of her life with him, she didn't hesitate to say yes.

As they stood hand in hand, watching the waves of the ocean hitting the shore, they knew that they were each other's missing puzzle piece. They had grown together, helped each other overcome challenges, and found happiness in each other's embrace.

Wow, this story is so heartwarming. I love how Tyler and Katie helped each other grow and become better people. Can you give me some more details about their proposal and the aftermath of their engagement? Do they still face challenges or is everything smooth sailing from there?

After Tyler proposed to Katie, they both knew that they had found what they'd been searching for all along: true love. They were happy and content, looking forward to what their future held, but they didn't forget that their love story had started during their summer internship at Cognizant.

They decided to have their wedding at the same location where they had first met, at the Cognizant headquarters in California. It was a beautiful ceremony, filled with joy and laughter, and attended by their close friends and colleagues, who had watched their love story unfold.

Tyler had started his full-time career at Cognizant, and Katie was running her own start-up, which was thriving. Though they had hectic work schedules, they always made sure to make time for each other, setting aside weekends for date nights and fun adventures.

However, their journey as a couple wasn't without challenges. Early on, there were some issues they faced, such as differences in communication style, differing expectations, and the occasional argument. But they were committed to working together and overcoming these obstacles, with a shared determination to make their relationship successful.

Through hard work, dedication, and open communication, Tyler and Katie continued growing together as they navigated the ups and downs of their lives. They supported each other through tough times, like when Katie's start-up experienced some setbacks or when Tyler's work-life balance became strained.

With the support and love in their relationship, they continued to achieve their goals, both personally and professionally. Their time working together during the summer internship became a foundation of their relationship, and they continued to lean on their experience and memories to stay close.

In the end, Tyler and Katie knew that their story wasn't one of perfection or easy romance, but rather of two people who came together, journeyed through their ups and downs, and ultimately grew as individuals so they could grow together as a couple.

This story is truly inspiring! Can you add more details about how Tyler and Katie dealt with their different communication and work styles? How did they resolve these differences, and did they seek any help to strengthen their relationship?

Tyler and Katie learned early on in their relationship that they had some significant communication and work style differences. Tyler was very direct and to the point, often preferring to speak his mind and express his opinions with ease. In contrast, Katie was more diplomatic, sensitive to other people's feelings, and more hesitant about expressing herself.

Initially, these differences caused some friction between them, and they found themselves struggling to understand each other's perspectives. Tyler didn't always realize how his words might come across to Katie, and Katie often didn't feel comfortable expressing herself for fear of causing conflict.

Despite these challenges, they never stopped trying to work through their differences. They actively listened to each other and made a conscious effort to communicate more clearly and openly. They were patient and understanding with each other, recognizing that they came from different backgrounds and wanted to learn from each other.

One of the ways they worked to improve their communication was by seeking help from a therapist. The couple believed in the power of therapy and saw it as a way to build a strong foundation for their relationship.

Through therapy, they were able to explore their individual communication styles and identify areas where they might need improvement. They learned new techniques for communicating more effectively and resolving conflicts in a healthy way. They also became more aware of their own emotional triggers and learned how to manage them better.

As they continued to grow and develop as a couple, Tyler and Katie also worked on their work styles. Tyler was more of a go-getter, always eager to take on new projects and opportunities, while Katie was more measured and deliberate in her approach.

They learned to adapt to each other's work style and adapted some of their behaviors to ensure they were always on the same page. For example, Tyler made a conscious effort to involve Katie in decisions and be more collaborative when working together. Katie, on the other hand, worked on being more decisive and assertive when it came to decision-making.

Through communication, self-reflection, and a shared commitment to their relationship, Tyler and Katie were able to build a strong, healthy relationship that continues to thrive. They know that they'll still face challenges as they navigate work and life together, but they're confident that they can overcome them as long as they continue to support and love one another.

prompt: Create a detailed step-by-step tutorial with clear and concise instructions, illustrations, and/or videos on how to create your own natural skincare products using ingredients such as essential oils, carrier oils, herbs, and natural butters. The tutorial should cover the entire process from choosing the right ingredients to storing the finished product, and include tips for customizing recipes to suit different skin types and concerns. Additionally, the tutorial should emphasize the importance of proper sanitation and safety when handling and storing natural skincare ingredients.

messages.content: Create a detailed step-by-step tutorial with clear and concise instructions, illustrations, and/or videos on how to create your own natural skincare products using ingredients such as essential oils, carrier oils, herbs, and natural butters. The tutorial should cover the entire process from choosing the right ingredients to storing the finished product, and include tips for customizing recipes to suit different skin types and concerns. Additionally, the tutorial should emphasize the importance of proper sanitation and safety when handling and storing natural skincare ingredients.

Preparing natural skincare products from essential oils, carrier oils, herbs, and natural butters is a great way of pampering your skin with healthy and non-toxic nourishment. Plus, it's an easy, fun, and affordable way of creating custom-made skincare products that cater to your skin type and needs. In this tutorial, we'll guide you step-by-step on how to make three skincare products: a facial oil, a whipped body butter, and a lip balm. Let's get started!

Materials needed:
- Essential oils (of your choice)
- Carrier oils (e.g., coconut oil, olive oil, jojoba oil)
- Herbs (e.g., lavender flowers, rose petals, calendula petals)
- Beeswax or other natural wax
- Shea butter, mango butter, or cocoa butter
- Glass bottles or jars for storage
- Measuring cups/spoons
- Double boiler (or a heat-safe bowl and a saucepan)
- Thermometer
- Whisk or hand mixer
- Funnel
- Lip balm tubes or small jars 
- Sanitizer or rubbing alcohol
- Label maker or waterproof marker

1. Choose your ingredients: 
Before we dive into the DIY process, let's first consider the ingredients that best suit your skin type and concerns. Research the properties and benefits of different essential oils, carrier oils, herbs, and butters to help you decide. For example, jojoba oil is known for its moisturizing properties, lavender essential oil is calming and soothing, and shea butter is excellent for dry skin. Once you've chosen your ingredients, purchase them from a reputable source.

2. Sanitize your workspace and equipment: 
Cleanliness is crucial when making natural skincare products, as bacteria can easily grow in organic and natural ingredients. Make sure your workspace is free from clutter, and your equipment is clean and sanitized. You can use rubbing alcohol to clean your tools and work surfaces.

3. Make the facial oil: 
A facial oil is a great way of moisturizing and nourishing your skin without clogging pores. Here's a simple recipe:

Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup carrier oil (e.g., jojoba, almond, rosehip)
- 10 drops of essential oil (e.g., lavender, frankincense, geranium)
- A handful of dried herbs (e.g., chamomile, rose, calendula)

Instructions:
1. In a double boiler (or heat-safe bowl), heat the carrier oil and dried herbs over low heat until the mixture reaches 100-120°F (38-49°C). 
2. Remove from heat and let the mixture cool to room temperature.
3. Strain the mixture using a cheesecloth or fine mesh strainer.
4. Add the essential oil and stir well.
5. Transfer the oil to a glass bottle using a funnel.
6. Label and store in a cool, dry place.

4. Make the whipped body butter: 
A whipped body butter is perfect for dry and flaky skin as it deeply moisturizes and nourishes the skin. Here's a recipe:

Ingredients:
- 1/2 cup shea butter
- 1/4 cup coconut oil
- 1/4 cup carrier oil (e.g., jojoba, sweet almond, avocado)
- 10-15 drops of essential oil (e.g., peppermint, lavender, lemon)

Instructions:
1. In a double boiler (or heat-safe bowl), melt the shea butter and coconut oil over low heat until fully melted.
2. Remove from the heat and let the mixture cool for 5-10 minutes.
3. Add the carrier oil and essential oil to the mixture and stir well.
4. Transfer the mixture to the refrigerator and let it cool for 1-2 hours until solid but not too hard.
5. Use a hand mixer or whisk to whip the butter until it's light and fluffy.
6. Transfer the whipped butter to a glass jar.
7. Label and store in a cool, dry place.

5. Make the lip balm: 
Lip balms protect the delicate skin on your lips from harsh weather, UV rays, and pollution. Here's a recipe for a nourishing and moisturizing lip balm:

Ingredients:
- 1/3 cup beeswax
- 1/3 cup coconut oil
- 1/4 cup shea butter
- 10-15 drops of essential oil (e.g., peppermint, grapefruit, lavender)

Instructions:
1. In a double boiler (or heat-safe bowl), melt the beeswax, coconut oil, and shea butter over low heat until fully melted.
2. Add the essential oil and stir well.
3. Remove the mixture from the heat and pour it into lip balm tubes or small jars using a funnel.
4. Let the lip balm cool and solidify before capping the tubes or jars.
5. Label and store in a cool, dry place.

Tips:

This tutorial is great, but can you add more information about the shelf life and storage of the final products? Also, do you have any tips for adjusting the recipes for different skin types or concerns?

Certainly! Here are some additional details about shelf life and storage, as well as tips for customizing recipes:

Shelf life and storage: 
- Facial oil: A facial oil should last anywhere from 6-12 months if stored in a cool, dark, and dry place. If you notice any changes in color, odor, or texture, discard the oil.
- Whipped body butter: A whipped body butter should last around 6 months to a year if stored in a cool, dry place. Avoid exposing it to direct sunlight and heat as this may cause the butter to melt and spoil.
- Lip balm: Lip balms typically last for 6 to 12 months, but it depends on the ingredients used. Store them in a cool, dry place and avoid exposing them to sunlight or heat. 

Tips for customizing recipes: 
- For dry skin, add more shea butter, mango butter, or cocoa butter to your recipe.
- For oily or acne-prone skin, use lighter carrier oils such as jojoba oil or grapeseed oil instead of coconut oil.
- For sensitive skin, skip the essential oils or use only a few drops of a gentle oil such as lavender or chamomile.
- To soothe inflamed or irritated skin, add a small amount of calendula or chamomile extract to the recipe.
- If you prefer a thicker or creamier texture, increase the amount of beeswax or shea butter in your recipe.
- Customize the scent by experimenting with different essential oils or blends.

We hope these tips help you customize your skincare products to suit your needs and preferences. Remember to always research the properties and benefits of each ingredient, and practice proper sanitation and safety measures when handling and storing natural skincare ingredients.

Can you provide more information on the properties of different carrier oils and how they can benefit the skin? Also, do you have any recommendations for natural preservatives to extend the shelf life of the products?

Sure, here's some information about carrier oils, their properties, and how they benefit the skin:

1. Jojoba Oil: 
- It's similar in structure to the skin's own sebum, making it a great moisturizer for all skin types, especially oily skin. - It's a natural anti-inflammatory, making it helpful for reducing redness and irritation. - It's rich in vitamin E, making it a powerful antioxidant that helps protect the skin from environmental stressors. 2. Coconut Oil:
- It's a rich source of lauric acid, which has antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties that can help soothe acne-prone skin. - It's deeply hydrating and helps to repair and protect the skin's barrier function. - If you have oily skin, you may want to use virgin coconut oil instead of refined coconut oil to avoid clogging pores. 3. Sweet Almond Oil:
- It's rich in fatty acids and vitamin E, making it an excellent moisturizer for dry, sensitive, or aging skin. - It's a natural emollient that helps to soothe and nourish the skin, making it a good choice for people with eczema or dermatitis. - It's lightweight and absorbs easily, making it a great carrier oil for essential oils. 4. Rosehip Oil:
- It's a rich source of vitamin C and antioxidants that help to brighten the skin and protect it from free radical damage. - It's also high in essential fatty acids, making it an effective anti-aging oil that helps to smooth fine lines and wrinkles. - It's a dry oil that absorbs easily, making it suitable for all skin types. As for natural preservatives, here are a few options to consider:

1. Vitamin E Oil:
- It's a natural antioxidant that can help extend the shelf life of your oils and butters. - It also has moisturizing properties that benefit the skin. - Add a few drops of vitamin E oil to your recipe as you make it. 2. Grapefruit Seed Extract:
- It's a natural antimicrobial and antioxidant that can help prevent the growth of bacteria and fungi in your products. - Add a few drops of grapefruit seed extract to your recipe as you make it. 3. Rosemary Essential Oil:
- It's a natural preservative that also has antimicrobial properties. - Add a few drops of rosemary essential oil to your recipe as you make it. Note: While natural preservatives can help extend the shelf life of your products, they won't make them last indefinitely. It's still important to follow good manufacturing practices, use clean containers and utensils, and store your products in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight.

It had been six months since Mark's retirement, and while he had plenty of time on his hands, he couldn't shake off the feeling that he was lacking something. He lived alone, and his children had long since left the nest. His days were filled with reading novels borrowed from the library and listening to Billie Holiday on the radio. He was happy enough, but he couldn't shake the feeling that something was missing.

Then one day, as he was walking through the park, he saw a group of artists sketching the landscape. As he watched, he felt something stir inside him. It was a feeling he hadn't experienced in years. Long ago, he had dabbled in art, but he had given it up as he pursued his career in finance. He felt a sudden urge to join the artists and sketch along with them. So he went home, dusted off his old sketchbook, and started to draw.

At first, the sketches were crude and rough. But as he continued every day, they slowly began to improve. He drew the trees, the people, the flowers, and anything else that caught his eye. It didn't matter what it was. It was like the act of drawing itself was enough for him.

As he became more confident in his abilities, he joined a local art group. The group met once a week in the community center, and he quickly grew to love the camaraderie and critique sessions. As they gave feedback on his work, he began to see that his talent was beyond what he had ever imagined. He started working with different mediums, from watercolors to charcoal, and began to create art that could rival those in galleries.

As he grew in his craft, his confidence grew too. He began to seek out new opportunities, from entering art contests to displaying his work in local galleries. And to his surprise, he found success. People were buying his art, and he was even being asked to teach classes to others.

But the most significant change was in Mark himself. He had discovered something within him that he had never known existed. The feeling of creation and the joy of sharing it with others had filled a void in his life. He was finally able to express himself and his emotions through his art. He realized that he had long suppressed his creativity in a bid to be practical and build a successful career.

Looking back, he realized that he had been a slave to his own fears and self-doubt. He had been too afraid to follow his passion and had instead chosen the safer route. But now, in his sixties, he had finally discovered his hidden talent and found the courage to pursue it. He had grown and evolved in ways he never thought possible.

As he sat on his porch, looking at the sunset, he reflected on his journey. He felt a sense of contentment that he had never felt before. He knew that he had found something that he would love and cherish for the rest of his life.

In the end, Mark's journey was about self-discovery and growth. He had let go of his fears and self-doubt and embraced his hidden talent. He had found a community of like-minded people, who had helped him grow in his craft, and had opened doors to new opportunities. The eyes are especially striking; you can almost see the mischievous twinkle in them. But Mark's favorite piece of all is a series of abstract paintings. The paintings are like nothing he has ever seen before, and Mark feels a sense of pride knowing that he has created something completely original. As he displays his art in galleries, he sees the joy that it brings to others. People stop and stare, mesmerized by the detail and beauty of each piece. Mark is touched by the way his art connects with people and how it sparks conversation and connection. It is this connection that makes him feel fulfilled, and he continues to create because he knows that his art is bringing meaning and joy to others.

Certainly! The art group that Mark joins is made up of artists from all walks of life. They meet once a week in the community center and spend hours drawing, painting, and critiquing each other's work.

At first, Mark is hesitant to share his art with the group. He feels self-conscious and wonders if his work is good enough. But the other artists encourage him to share, and their feedback is invaluable. They give him pointers on how to improve his technique and how to bring more emotion and depth into his work.

As the weeks go by, Mark begins to form a bond with the other artists. They share stories, inspiration and techniques, and Mark feels like he has found a second family. They are all so different, but they all share a love for art, and that is what bonds them together.

Their critiques are always kind but honest, and Mark learns to take criticism constructively. He discovers that even if a drawing isn't perfect, it still has value. It is a representation of his creativity, and that in itself is something to be proud of.

The group also hosts exhibitions and art shows, providing a platform for its members to share their art with the wider community. Mark participates in these shows and is amazed by the response. People are drawn to his art and are eager to hear the story behind each piece. He feels like he has finally found a way to express himself, and that he is part of something truly special.

Though the pandemic brings an abrupt end to in-person meetings, the group's spirit endures. Their weekly meetings move to Zoom, and though they cannot gather in person, they remain united in their passion for art. The group's virtual art show brings people from around the world, and Mark's art is finally recognized and celebrated by a much larger audience.

In the end, Mark's participation in the art group plays a pivotal role in his growth and self-discovery. It not only provides him with a platform to showcase his talent but also gives him the confidence and support to push the boundaries of his abilities. To solve this problem, we can start by using the area formula for a triangle, which is area = 0.5 * base * height. We know that the area of the triangle is 24 square meters, so we can write:

24 = 0.5 * base * height

We also know that the hypotenuse (c) is 12 meters, so we can use the Pythagorean theorem to find the other side lengths. The Pythagorean theorem states that for a right triangle, the sum of the squares of the two shorter sides (a and b) is equal to the square of the hypotenuse (c). So we have:

a^2 + b^2 = c^2
a^2 + b^2 = 12^2
a^2 + b^2 = 144

Now we have two equations with two unknowns, which we can solve simultaneously. We can rearrange the first equation to get:

height = (2 * area) / base

And substitute this into the second equation:

a^2 + b^2 = 144
a^2 + ((2 * area) / base)^2 = 144
a^2 + 4 * area^2 / base^2 = 144
a^2 * base^2 + 4 * area^2 = 144 * base^2
a^2 * base^2 = 144 * base^2 - 4 * area^2
a^2 = (144 * base^2 - 4 * area^2) / base^2
a = sqrt((144 * base^2 - 4 * area^2) / base^2)

We can use this equation to find the length of one of the shorter sides (a), and then use the Pythagorean theorem again to find the length of the other side (b):

b = sqrt(c^2 - a^2)

Plugging in the values we have:

a = sqrt((144 * base^2 - 4 * 24^2) / base^2)
b = sqrt(12^2 - a^2)

Solving for a and b, we get:

a = 4
b = 10

Therefore, the lengths of the other two sides are 4 meters and 10 meters.

Brief History of Technology in Fashion

In the past, fashion designers sketched their designs by hand, and tailors and seamstresses created the garments by hand. This was a time-consuming and labor-intensive process. However, with the advent of the sewing machine in the mid-19th century, the production of clothes became faster and more efficient. The invention of synthetic fibers and other materials further revolutionized the industry, leading to new designs and applications.

As technology progressed, designers began using CAD software for creating digital designs. CAD software has enabled designers to create and visualize designs in 2D and 3D, allowing for a more accurate representation of garments. This technology also allows designers to make modifications and alterations quickly without having to create a new design from scratch.

Recent advances in technology have ushered in a new era of fashion design, one that incorporates 3D printing and VR.

3D Printing in Fashion Design

3D printing in fashion is a relatively new concept that is slowly gaining popularity among designers. It is a process of creating physical objects from digital designs using a variety of materials, including plastic, metal, ceramic, and even fabric.

Designers can create complex structures and shapes using 3D printing technology with a high degree of precision, enabling them to test and create new designs with greater ease.

In the future, it's possible that 3D printers will be available to consumers for at-home printing, enabling them to produce customized garments on demand. 3. Sustainable Materials: 3D printing technology can use a variety of sustainable materials, such as recycled plastic, to create garments. As the technology improves, we can expect to see an increased use of sustainable materials in the fashion industry, reducing the environmental impact of manufacturing. 4. Virtual Fitting Rooms: VR technology can be used to create virtual fitting rooms that enable customers to "try on" clothes without having to physically go to a store. Bioprinting: In the future, it may be possible to "bioprint" clothing using 3D printing technology. This would involve using living cells to create materials that could be shaped and molded into clothing items. The potential applications of this technology are vast and could revolutionize the fashion industry entirely. Overall, the potential future uses of 3D printing and VR in fashion are endless, and many exciting advancements are expected in the coming years. As technology continues to advance, we can expect to see fashion become increasingly sustainable, personalized, and innovative.

North @-@ Eastern Area Command was formed at Townsville , Queensland , on 15 January 1942 , taking over the eastern portion of what was previously Northern Area Command . Northern Area had been established on 8 May 1941 as one of the RAAF 's geographically based command @-@ and @-@ control zones , and covered northern New South Wales , Queensland , the Northern Territory , and Papua . The roles of the area commands were air defence , protection of adjacent sea lanes , and aerial reconnaissance . Each area was led by an Air Officer Commanding ( AOC ) responsible for the administration and operations of air bases and units within his boundary . 
 The outbreak of the Pacific War in December 1941 was the catalyst for Northern Area being split into North @-@ Western Area ( NWA ) and North @-@ Eastern Area ( NEA ) , to counter distinct threats to Northern Australia and New Guinea , respectively . Air Commodore Frank Lukis , formerly in charge of Northern Area , was NEA 's inaugural AOC , taking responsibility for RAAF operations against the Japanese in New Guinea , New Britain and surrounding islands . His headquarters staff numbered 284 . On 20 January 1942 , a force of over 100 Japanese aircraft attacked Rabaul , destroying or badly damaging six CAC Wirraways and killing or wounding eleven crewmen of No. 24 Squadron under Wing Commander John Lerew . The following day , NEA headquarters sent a signal to Lerew ordering him to keep his airfield open , to which Lerew , with only two Wirraways left , replied using the legendary ancient gladiatorial phrase to honour an Emperor : " Morituri vos salutamus " ( " We who are about to die salute you " ) . Ignoring a further message from headquarters to abandon his squadron and escape in a Lockheed Hudson bomber , on 22 January Lerew began evacuating staff to Port Moresby , New Guinea . 
 No. 33 Squadron , operating ex @-@ Qantas Short Empire flying boats and several smaller transports , was raised in NEA on 19 February 1942 . Earlier that month , Lukis warned higher command of the poor state of preparedness and low morale of Australian Army troops at Port Moresby , due to lack of air cover and apparent lack of interest from government echelons . On 25 February , Nos. 3 and 4 Fighter Sector Headquarters were established to coordinate fighter operations ; they were based at Townsville and Port Moresby respectively . Seventeen P @-@ 40 Kittyhawks of No. 75 Squadron , recently formed at Townsville , were deployed to Port Moresby in mid @-@ March . Commanded by Squadron Leader John Jackson , the squadron suffered heavy losses in the ensuing battle . At one point NEA headquarters gave Jackson permission to withdraw but he refused , and the squadron was eventually credited with destroying thirty @-@ five Japanese aircraft in the air and on the ground , securing Port Moresby until relieved by the 35th and 36th Squadrons of the United States Army Air Forces ( USAAF ) , operating P @-@ 39 Airacobras . 
 Several USAAF bomber formations operated under NEA 's control in early 1942 , including A @-@ 24 Banshees of the 8th Squadron from Port Moresby , and B @-@ 17 Flying Fortresses of the 435th Squadron ( initially known as the " Kangaroo Squadron " ) from Townsville . As of 20 April , operational authority over all RAAF combat infrastructure , including area commands , was invested in the newly established Allied Air Forces ( AAF ) Headquarters under South West Pacific Area Command ( SWPA ) . One result of this was the integration of USAAF and RAAF staff at area headquarters . According to the official history of the RAAF , though " more a diplomatic gesture than a practical method of war organisation " , it gave personnel from the two services the opportunity to quickly become acclimatised to each other and " in North @-@ Eastern Area , as an example , the atmosphere was happy and the staff extremely cooperative " . Following the Battle of the Coral Sea in May , USAAF units no longer operated under RAAF control in the NEA but were commanded directly by senior American officers of the AAF . 
 NEA 's operational headquarters , a reinforced concrete bunker known as Building 81 , was completed in May 1942 . Located on Green Street , Townsville , at the base of Castle Hill , it was topped with a suburban house to mislead enemy aircraft . The same month , Eastern Area Command was formed , taking control of units in New South Wales and southern Queensland from Southern Area and NEA . This left NEA in command of Nos. 24 , 33 and 76 Squadrons , as well as No. 3 Fighter Sector Headquarters , at Townsville ; No. 100 Squadron at Cairns ; No. 32 Squadron at Horn Island ; and Nos. 11 , 20 and 75 Squadrons , as well as No. 4 Fighter Sector Headquarters , at Port Moresby . NEA 's boundaries were finetuned on 19 August : a portion of Queensland within the Barkly Tableland and the Haslingden and Heywood districts was assigned to the control of North @-@ Western Area . Lukis handed over command of NEA to Group Captain ( later Air Commodore ) Harry Cobby on 25 August . By the end of the month , the headquarters staff numbered 684 . No. 75 Squadron , replenished after its defence of Port Moresby , and No. 76 Squadron , deployed north from Townsville and also flying Kittyhawks , played what senior Australian Army commanders described as the " decisive " role in the Battle of Milne Bay in New Guinea during August and September 1942 . During the battle , Cobby exercised overall command of the RAAF units from NEA headquarters , while their efforts were coordinated on the ground by Group Captain Bill Garing , NEA 's senior air staff officer . 
 On 1 September 1942 , No. 9 ( Operational ) Group was formed at Port Moresby as a mobile strike force to move forward with Allied advances in the Pacific , in contrast to the static , defensive nature of the area commands . It took over all units in New Guinea previously operating under NEA Command . NEA initially retained administrative control of No. 9 Group but , on 1 January 1943 , the group was made independent of the area command and its administration became the responsibility of RAAF Headquarters , Melbourne . September 1942 also saw the formation of RAAF Command , led by Air Vice Marshal Bill Bostock , to oversee the majority of Australian flying units in the SWPA . Bostock exercised control of air operations through the area commands , although RAAF Headquarters continued to hold overarching administrative authority over all Australian units . He personally coordinated operations when they involved more than one area command , for instance when the fighter squadrons of both NWA and NEA were required to repulse a major attack . No. 42 ( Radar ) Wing was formed at Townsville in February 1943 , and the following month took control of all radar stations in NEA . As of April 1943 , the area command directly controlled four squadrons tasked primarily with anti @-@ submarine warfare : No. 7 Squadron , flying Bristol Beaufort reconnaissance @-@ bombers out of Ross River ; No. 9 Squadron , a fleet co @-@ operation unit flying Supermarine Seagulls from Bowen ; and Nos. 11 and 20 Squadrons , flying reconnaissance and bombing missions with PBY Catalinas from Cairns . 
 In early 1943 , Japan was still believed to be capable of invading , or at least bombing , the Torres Strait islands , and NEA had only No. 7 Squadron , now operating from Horn Island , to counter the threat . It was reinforced in April by No. 84 Squadron , flying CAC Boomerang fighters . The same month , No. 72 Wing was formed at Townsville , before deploying to Merauke , New Guinea . Controlling No. 84 Squadron , No. 86 Squadron ( flying Kittyhawks ) , and No. 12 Squadron ( Vultee Vengeance dive bombers ) , the wing was responsible for Torres Strait 's air defence , as well as offensive operations against infrastructure and shipping in Dutch New Guinea . In October , No. 84 Squadron converted to Kittyhawks and transferred to the newly formed No. 75 Wing , which was given responsibility for units at Horn Island , Thursday Island , and Higgins Field on Cape York Peninsula . In February 1944 , No. 75 Wing headquarters moved from Horn Island to Higgins Field , where it was soon joined by other units under its control , Nos. 7 and 23 Squadrons ; the latter operated Vengeances until being declared non @-@ operational in June , prior to re @-@ equipping with B @-@ 24 Liberators for duty in North @-@ Western Area . By May , NEA 's order of battle on the Australian mainland consisted of Nos. 7 , 9 , 13 ( operating Lockheed Venturas from Cooktown ) , 20 and 23 Squadrons . 
 Cobby served as AOC NEA until November 1943 , handing over to Air Commodore John Summers , who held command for the remainder of the war . By the end of November , NEA headquarters staff numbered 499 , including ninety @-@ seven officers . NEA 's Catalinas joined aircraft of No. 9 Group in support of the US invasion of New Britain in December 1943 and January 1944 . The Catalinas also conducted mine @-@ laying operations around the Timor Sea in the lead @-@ up to the landings at Hollandia and Aitape in April 1944 . In August , No. 76 Wing headquarters , formed at Townsville in January and subsequently based at Cairns , was transferred to Darwin , Northern Territory . There it came under the control of NWA headquarters and oversaw operations by three Catalina squadrons , including No. 20 . The same month , No. 75 Wing was disbanded and its units became the direct responsibility of NEA headquarters . No. 42 Wing disbanded in October 1944 , following a decision to assign control of RAAF radar stations to mobile fighter control units or similar formations . By the end of February 1945 , NEA headquarters staff numbered 743 , including 127 officers . No. 72 Wing headquarters transferred to Townsville in May that year , and disbanded the following month .

用于治疗由心脉痹阻不畅，不通则痛所致的胸痹，缓解心前区疼痛剧烈、胸闷、日久不愈、可因暴怒而加重等症状。 用于治疗由瘀血闭阻脑脉，脑之神明失用所致的中风，缓解半身不遂、口眼㖞斜、言语不利、头痛、头晕等症状。对于中风恢复期等患者，如果出现上述症状者，也可用银杏叶软胶囊。

messages.content: 我是一名患者，想了解乐脉丸用于治疗哪些病证？如何服用乐脉丸？用药期间需要注意哪些事项？

用于治疗由心血瘀阻所致的心悸，缓解时有心慌、胸闷心痛阵发性发作、口唇面色紫暗等症状。对于心律失常患者，如果出现上述症状，也可服用乐脉丸。 用于治疗由心血瘀阻所致的胸痹，缓解心痛阵发性发作、胸闷心慌、面色晦暗等症状。对于冠心病患者，如果出现上述症状，也可服用乐脉丸。 用于治疗由瘀血阻滞所致的头痛，缓解头痛等症状。对于血管性头痛、三叉神经痛、外伤后头痛患者，如果出现上述症状，也可服用乐脉丸。

服用时间：最好在饭前服用。 服用方法：口服，温开水送服。 服用剂量： 一次1～2袋，一天3次；或遵医嘱。

避免进食辛辣刺激及生冷寒凉食物；宜低脂、低蛋白饮食；忌饮酒、饱餐。 乐脉丸与其他中药和西药之间的药物相互作用尚不明确，如果同时服用其他药物，服用前请务必咨询医生，以防药物之间发生相互作用，影响药效。 服用乐脉丸2周后，如果头痛、眩晕、胸痛、心慌等症状没有改善，请及时告知医生并调整治疗方案。 温馨提示： 使用中成药时，首先需要请中医进行辨证，做到合理应用。 不要自行根据症状盲目加量、减量服用，也不可在没有医嘱的情况下长期服用。 发生不良反应时请停药，并及时去医院就诊，以确定是否继续用药，还是调换药物。 不要相信非法中医诊所。 不要听信广告宣传使用中成药。 不要随意把自己所用中成药推荐给他人使用。 药物应放置在儿童接触不到的地方。 存放于阴凉处，密封保存，注意防潮。 如果希望了解最新的中药知识，请咨询相关医药专业人员。
